title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 124
paragraphs: And he, upon hearing this, prepared to set out there, though the diviners and his friends strongly dissuaded him, and in spite, moreover, of a vision his daughter had seen in her sleep, of this kind: it seemed to her that her father was raised up on high and was bathed by Zeus and anointed by the Sun. Having seen this vision, she used every effort to dissuade Polycrates from leaving his land to go to Oroetes; and as he was embarking on his fifty-oared galley, she accompanied his departure with words of prophecy. He threatened her that if he came back safe, she should remain unmarried for a long time; but she prayed it might be so, for she would rather, she said, be unmarried for a long time than be an orphan, having lost her father.
